units.RK-10.2-007: BroadcastResult is what the pipeline's own broadcast() returns: no public call hands it out, so a scenario reads its members only through the units that produce them (deliveries, reentry events, tasks, observations, per-channel errors).
units.RK-10.3-020: The unit binds an implementation that accepts another edit_source. Both implementations refuse any value but sender, system and null as the content is built, so the case never arises in a runner: a scenario that passes another value sees the build's refusal, never a check as the sender's.
units.RK-10.6-009: The TurnBackend interface (submit, control, serve, close) is the shape of an object no step calls: its owner-side and executor-side messages lie below the public API a scenario drives (as for RK-10.6.3-009). units.RK-10.6.1-010: This sets what the backend does not carry and obliges nothing a scenario can see: a speech-to-speech channel's model holds the conversation in the owner's process, so it has no intelligence turn for a backend to carry, and the fan-out of an event to another process's live connections belongs to a deployment.
units.RK-10.6.1-011: The serialized messages a backend carries lie below the public API a scenario drives: no step reads or writes a link message, which a backend's own tests do. The same scenarios run on the in-memory and a distributed backend show only that the outcomes agree.

units.RK-10.6.1-013: That nothing changes a request's events in place is a property of the language objects the owner and the executor hold: no scripted hook or channel changes a record in place, and a hook's modify returns a new one.
units.RK-10.6.1-015: Whether an implementation keeps a local shortcut to the channel's objects is its internal structure: a scenario sees the turn's outcome, which a shortcut and the backend give alike.
units.RK-10.6.1-016: Holds of the suite as a whole, not of one scenario: every scenario of an intelligence channel runs through the in-memory backend, and their receipts are the evidence.
